items.rationale: A dull edge does not bite, so you push harder and the blade can skid off the food toward your hand. A sharp knife needs little force. Picking d shows M1, that a dull knife is safer.
Honing realigns an edge that has folded over with use; it removes almost no metal. Making a new edge is sharpening, so picking a shows M2, that honing sharpens a knife.
If honing no longer restores the cut, the edge is worn and metal must be removed on a whetstone or sharpener to form a new edge. Answering honing again shows M2.
Hand wash right away, with the blade's edge facing away from your wiping hand, then dry. Soaking or a loose pile in the sink hides the blade, and dishwashers bang and dull it.
A block or magnetic strip holds the blade where it cannot touch other metal or your hand. A loose drawer dulls the edge and cuts reaching fingers.

accepted: The blade is hidden under the water and you could cut yourself

items.rationale: A hidden blade is the main danger: a hand feeling around in cloudy water meets the edge. Soaking also damages handles, but the safety reason is the point.
